title: Unit Test: Metals and Non-metals
subject: Science
instructions: Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks.
Word equations are enough unless a chemical equation is asked for.

questions.q: Which metal is so soft that it can be cut with a knife?
A solution of which non-metal is applied on wounds as an antiseptic?
Which non-metal do we take in when we breathe?
Coating iron with a layer of zinc is called:
The green coating on copper vessels left in moist air is:
options: a mixture of copper hydroxide and copper carbonate
questions.answer: (d) a mixture of copper hydroxide and copper carbonate

questions.q: Which gas is produced when metals react with dilute acids?
Why are electric wires made of copper, but covered with plastic?
questions.answer: Copper is a good conductor of electricity (and ductile). Plastic is an insulator, so the covering protects us from electric shocks.

questions.q: Why should lemon pickle not be stored in aluminium or iron containers?
questions.answer: Lemon pickle contains acids, which react with metals. This spoils the pickle (harmful substances may form) and damages the container.

questions.q: An iron nail is placed in copper sulphate solution. What do you observe, and what does it show?
questions.answer: The blue colour of the solution fades and turns greenish, and a reddish-brown coating of copper forms on the nail. This shows that iron is more reactive than copper: it displaces copper.

questions.q: Give two uses each of metals and non-metals.
questions.answer: Metals (any two): machinery, cooking utensils, electric wires, jewellery, automobiles. Non-metals (any two): oxygen for breathing; nitrogen and phosphorus in fertilisers; chlorine to purify water; iodine as an antiseptic.

questions.q: Write word equations for what happens when: (i) sodium is put in water, (ii) a magnesium ribbon burns in air, (iii) sulphur burns in air.
questions.answer: (i) Sodium + water → sodium hydroxide + hydrogen (plus a lot of heat). (ii) Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide. (iii) Sulphur + oxygen → sulphur dioxide.

questions.q: The ash of a burnt magnesium ribbon is dissolved in water, and so is the gas from burning sulphur. Each solution is tested with litmus. What do you observe, and what can you conclude?
questions.answer: The magnesium oxide solution turns red litmus blue, so it is basic. The sulphur dioxide solution turns blue litmus red, so it is acidic. Conclusion: metals form basic oxides and non-metals form acidic oxides.

subparts.q: What is a displacement reaction? Give two examples as word equations.
subparts.answer: A reaction in which a more reactive metal pushes out (displaces) a less reactive metal from its compound in solution. Examples: zinc + copper sulphate → zinc sulphate + copper; iron + copper sulphate → iron sulphate + copper.

subparts.q: Will a reaction take place in each case? Give a reason. (i) Iron + zinc sulphate solution (ii) Zinc + iron sulphate solution
subparts.answer: (i) No. Iron is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc. (ii) Yes. Zinc is more reactive than iron: zinc + iron sulphate → zinc sulphate + iron.
